key_insight: OmniAgent reframes long video understanding as an active reasoning process rather than a passive frame-by-frame scan. By iteratively observing, thinking, and acting, it aims to reduce unnecessary computation while improving query-focused understanding across modalities.
problem_solved: Existing long-video models often use a "watch-it-all" strategy, which makes compute cost grow with video length even when the task is simple. Interactive methods help somewhat, but many still depend on costly global pre-scanning and do not fully avoid length-dependent context overhead.
method: Models video understanding as a POMDP, enabling an Observation-Thought-Action loop for iterative decision-making.
Uses native omni-modal interaction so the agent can choose what to inspect next instead of uniformly processing all frames.
Reduces reliance on full-video pre-scanning by dynamically selecting relevant information based on the query and current context.
impact: For practitioners, this suggests a more scalable way to handle long videos and multi-modal inputs without paying the full cost of exhaustive processing. It is especially useful for building efficient agents that answer complex queries with less compute and better focus.

paper_title: Native Active Perception as Reasoning for Omni-Modal Understanding
paper_authors: Zhenghao Xing, Ruiyang Xu, Yuxuan Wang, Jinzheng He, Ziyang Ma
